cands.bio: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 10th District since September 2024, a Democrat. Born and raised in Newark. Previously on the Newark Municipal Council from 2018 to 2024, serving as council president from 2022. Worked in school-district personnel and as a public affairs manager at PSE&G.

controversies.text: Missed 3 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (0.4%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 2, 2026-06-23 to 2026-06-23.

On May 9, 2025, federal agents moved to arrest Newark Mayor Ras Baraka outside Delaney Hall during her oversight visit. McIver was indicted on three counts of assaulting or impeding federal officers. She pleaded not guilty and calls the case political intimidation. In August 2026 a Third Circuit panel, 2-1, let two counts proceed and sent the third back to the lower court. No verdict yet.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include Working Families Party, New Jersey Citizen Action, Emgage Action and Humane World Action Fund.

For her 2024 special election, Ballotpedia lists an endorsement from U.S. Sen. Cory Booker. In her own survey she also named Local 32BJ, Hotel Trades Union, SEIU, Collective PAC, the Essex and Union Democratic parties, and the Payne family (self-reported).

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from McIver on data centers, development and land use, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, school choice or teacher pay, policing and public-order penalties, or gun laws. We also found nothing showing she has declined or accepted any particular type of funding. Sources give conflicting accounts of her school-district job: Montclair Public Schools on her campaign site and Wikipedia, Willingboro Public Schools in her 2024 survey. Her campaign site and survey also mention work at Essex Regional Educational Services Commission. Her Ballotpedia survey gives no date for moving to or living in New Jersey beyond her Newark birth and upbringing.

votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.bio: Carmen Bucco is a New Jersey entrepreneur, a tailor and the owner of Bucco Couture. He has not held public office. He ran as a Republican for State Senate in 2023, Assembly in 2025, and U.S. House in the 10th District in 2024 (special and regular elections) and 2026.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Carmen Bucco holding public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development or land use, property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2023 through 2026. We found no endorsements for him. His birthplace is given only as New Jersey, with no city. We could not establish when or where he was raised beyond his foster-care upbringing and his Nutley High School graduation. His campaign website's front page includes his own message, but most of the page we received was unrelated spam content, so we used only the candidate's own text. His issue positions come from a 2024 campaign website quoted by Ballotpedia, written for a state legislative race.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia says he was born in New Jersey and graduated from Nutley High School in 1990, and he has run in New Jersey legislative and congressional races from 2023 to 2026.

score.why: Raised $8,931, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Tailor and owner of the small business Bucco Couture, and founder of a foundation called Bucco's Rising Stars. He has never held elected or appointed office, and he lost bids for State Senate, Assembly and U.S. House.
qual.why: He has real small-business ownership experience but no governing, legislative, legal or policy-staff background, and his several runs have not produced a record in office.

second-amendment.evidence: His 2024 campaign website, from his state legislative run, says he supports the Second Amendment and that the right to keep and bear arms 'should never be infringed upon.'

back-police-order.evidence: His 2024 campaign website says 'we must always support our police and first responders and need to be tough on violent crimes,' and that tying the hands of law enforcement endangers communities.
